How to use PDF to Text

  1. Open the tool box above and add your file, text, or values.

  3. Click the main button, review the result, and download or copy the output.

Features

  • Text extraction
  • Copy output
  • Download .txt
  • No upload required

Best way to use PDF to Text

PDF to Text extracts selectable text from digital PDFs. It is not OCR, so scanned image-only documents need a separate OCR tool.

Best for

  • Copying text from reports
  • Extracting readable content from digital PDFs
  • Creating plain-text notes from PDF documents

Example workflow

Example: upload a text-based report PDF and download a .txt file containing page-separated extracted text.

Quality notes

The tool gives a clear scanned-PDF message instead of silently returning an empty file.

Before you download

  • Check that the output format matches the website, form, or software where you will upload it.
  • Open the downloaded file once before final submission so you can confirm quality, page order, dimensions, and readability.
  • If the result is too large, use the related compression or resize tools instead of repeating the same step many times.
  • If the source file is password-protected, corrupted, scanned, or extremely large, use a desktop or specialist tool when browser processing is not enough.

Troubleshooting

  • If no text is found, the PDF is likely scanned or image-only.
  • Complex layouts may not preserve perfect reading order.
  • Password-protected PDFs should be unlocked first.

Common uses for PDF to Text

  • prepare documents for online forms
  • combine or clean scanned certificates
  • create smaller document files for sharing

Tips for better results

Use valid, unlocked PDF files where possible. For scanned PDFs, text extraction may need OCR because image-only pages do not contain selectable text.
